title: Compatibility & phased migration spec for legacy /v1 client paths (downgrade-safe adapters)
creator: Priya Shah
description: This ticket defines the product requirements, acceptance criteria, and phased rollout for client migration off legacy /v1 endpoints toward the unified inference API. The goal is to provide downgrade-safe adapter paths, clear client guidance, and telemetry gates so customers can opt-in, test, and complete migrations with minimal disruption.
background: We announced consolidation of multiple legacy endpoints into the unified inference surface. Past migration docs focused on endpoint removal timelines; engineering and support have requested an explicit compatibility/adaptor strategy that lets SDKs and self-hosted clients fall back safely during rollout windows. This ticket ties the PRD to release gates and rollback criteria.
scope:
- Design and publish a compatibility adapter spec for legacy /v1->/infer translation.
- Define phased rollout milestones, telemetry gates, and opt-in SDK flags.
- Create client-facing migration checklist and example code snippets for curl, Node, and Python.
- Acceptance criteria and contract tests for backward-compatible behavior.
- Post-rollout monitoring dashboard definition.
out_of_scope:
- Building full server-side adapter service for third-party managed customers (separate sales/enterprise project).
- Automated code rewrite tooling for customer repos (we will provide examples and a CLI in follow-up).
acceptance_criteria: Compatibility adapter spec published in Confluence with request/response mapping for all legacy fields
SDKs (node/python/go) include an opt-in flag --use-compat-adapter and pass contract tests in QA pipeline
No functional regressions: responses from adapter route must match legacy formats for 95% of our regression corpus within semantic thresholds
Telemetry gates implemented: migration rollout will not proceed to next phase until error-rate reduction and latency SLAs are within defined thresholds
Migration checklist and client guidance published on docs.redwood.ai with sample snippets and FAQ
Stakeholder sign-off (Eng, DX, Support, Legal) recorded in ticket comments
rollout_timeline: Phase 0 (Design & sign-off) — 2025-03-01 to 2025-03-21: publish spec, implement SDK flag, unit contract tests
Phase 1 (Internal canary) — 2025-03-22 to 2025-04-04: internal apps opt-in, monitor telemetry gates
Phase 2 (Public opt-in) — 2025-04-05 to 2025-04-25: external customers can enable adapter; provide migration support hours
Phase 3 (Enforced routing & deprecation notice) — 2025-04-26 to 2025-05-01: begin routing legacy traffic through adapter and publish firm deprecation date
Phase 4 (Sunset enforcement) — post 2025-05-01: legacy endpoints disabled per deprecation policy after customer notification window
migration_steps: Publish technical adapter mapping and edge-cases doc (Confluence link in 'links').
Ship SDK opt-in flag and test harness that validates legacy response shape against unified output.
Create 'compat-mode' feature flag in console for accounts to opt-in/out of adapter per route.
Run internal canary with infra team — collect regressions and false-positive rates.
Open public beta and collect customer feedback; schedule weekly syncs with pilot customers.
After meeting telemetry gates, roll adapter to broader population and publish deprecation timeline.
Post-deprecation: provide a 30-day grace window for emergency rollback; track any residual errors and ship hotfixes as necessary.
client_guidance_snippets: Curl example: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/compat -H 'Authorization: Bearer <KEY>' -d '{"input":"hello"}' // maps to unified /infer internally
Node SDK: const client = new Redwood({compatAdapter: true}); await client.generate({model: 'r-infer-1', prompt});

Python SDK: client = RedwoodClient(compat_adapter=True)
resp = client.generate(prompt='summary of ...')
Guidance: enable compat adapter flag locally, run integration tests, measure token cost and latency before enabling in production
monitoring_telemetry_gates: Error rate (5xx + mapping failures) must be <= 0.5% for 72h before expanding rollout
Median additional latency introduced by adapter must be < 25ms for 95th percentile of requests
Semantic divergence metric (regression corpus) must be <= 5% top-level failures over a 24h window
Cost delta per token observed and flagged if > 20% increase for sustained 24h period
rollback_criteria: Sustained error spike above 1% for > 30 minutes after mitigation attempts
Semantic regression > 8% on the regression corpus over a 24h window
Latency P95 increase > 100ms compared to pre-adapter baseline for > 1 hour
Any incident that causes data-loss or unexpected schema changes for customer payloads
open_questions: Should the adapter be offered as a server-side managed feature for enterprise customers (cost/SLAs)?
Do we need a lightweight telemetry SDK embedded in the adapter to capture semantic quality signals, or can we rely on existing logging pipelines?
What is the precise retention policy for adapter debug logs (security/legal asks)?
How do we surface adapter opt-in state in billing and cost dashboards?
